names.value: American Samoa — naval territorial administration

politicalStatus.value: US island dependency under naval administration

governments.value: Naval governor and territorial administration

descriptions.value: Tutuila/Aunuʻu and Manuʻa cessions occurred separately in 1900 and 1904; coverage begins conservatively in 1905. The later addition of Swains Island in 1925 and detailed local institutions remain partial.

politicalStatus.value: US territorial dependency under Interior supervision

governments.value: Governor-led territorial administration under the Department of the Interior

descriptions.value: Administration transferred from the Navy to Interior in 1951. Modern elected governorship and later constitutions are not projected into 1960; Fono record dates do not establish legislative powers for this year.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Fiji — British colonial framework

politicalStatus.value: British Crown colony

governments.value: British colonial governor

descriptions.value: The colony was established in 1874. This political core does not imply uniform practical control, universal representation or consensual indigenous sovereignty. The governor’s additional Western Pacific office changed in 1952; details remain uncurated. Independence in 1970 lies outside coverage.

names.value: Niue — New Zealand dependency

politicalStatus.value: Island dependency administered by New Zealand

governments.value: New Zealand resident commissioner

descriptions.value: The conservative 1902 start follows annexation in 1901; the months of the 1900 protectorate transition remain uncurated. Self-government and free association from 1974 are not projected into 1960.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Papua and New Guinea — administrative union in 1960

politicalStatus.value: Australian administrative union of Papua Crown possession and New Guinea UN trust territory

governments.value: Administrator governing on behalf of the Commonwealth of Australia

descriptions.value: Joint administration did not erase the separate legal status of the two territories. Earlier German, British and Australian administrations cannot be presented as a single political state. Detailed amendments to the 1960 council framework remain uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: German Samoa — western islands before occupation

politicalStatus.value: German colonial dependency

governments.value: German colonial administration

descriptions.value: The German framework applied to western Samoan islands following partition; eastern American Samoa was distinct. Local chiefly institutions and the 1905 reorganisation remain partial.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Western Samoa — New Zealand military occupation

politicalStatus.value: Occupied German dependency under New Zealand military administration

governments.value: New Zealand military administration

descriptions.value: Occupation began on 29 August 1914; January 1914 remained under German administration. Coverage ends before the May 1920 civil transition. Later League mandate and UN trusteeship institutions are not projected backwards.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Western Samoa — League of Nations mandate

politicalStatus.value: ClassC League of Nations mandate administered by New Zealand

governments.value: New Zealand Administrator with colonial legislative and chiefly advisory institutions

descriptions.value: The mandate was confirmed on 17 December 1920; a conservative 1921 start excludes the earlier civil transition. Council and faipule membership changed, so founding counts and unlimited local consent are not assumed. Mau resistance qualified practical authority.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Western Samoa — cabinet government within trusteeship

politicalStatus.value: Internally self-governing UN trust territory under New Zealand administration

governments.value: Samoan Prime Minister and cabinet, Legislative Assembly, and New Zealand High Commissioner

descriptions.value: Cabinet government began in October 1959. The 1960 constitutional preparations did not end trusteeship. Independence and joint sovereign heads of state from 1962 lie outside this core; exact reserved powers in 1960 remain uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Tonga — constitutional kingdom before British protection

politicalStatus.value: Independent constitutional monarchy

governments.value: King and constitutional royal government

descriptions.value: The constitution was introduced in 1875 after unification in 1845. The earlier Tuʻi Tonga Empire title and later British control of foreign affairs are not projected into this period. Detailed parliamentary franchise remains uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Tonga — protected constitutional kingdom

politicalStatus.value: Constitutional monarchy under British protection

governments.value: King and constitutional government with British intervention

descriptions.value: The 1900 arrangement gave Britain control of foreign affairs; subsequent internal intervention grew. This was not direct colonial annexation or unchanged complete autonomy. The conservative 1901 start leaves transition months uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Wallis and Futuna — French protectorate

politicalStatus.value: Unified French protectorate over distinct island chiefly systems

governments.value: French resident and protectorate administration

descriptions.value: A unified protectorate was created in 1888; the earlier islands are not automatically one polity. Royal appointments and the precise powers associated with the 1942 US base remain uncurated. The 1959 referendum did not establish the 1961 territorial assembly in 1960.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Commonwealth of Australia — pre-adoption federal framework

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing federal Commonwealth under the Crown with continuing imperial legal connections

governments.value: Governor-General, parliamentary ministry and bicameral Senate/House of Representatives

descriptions.value: Federation in 1901 did not immediately remove all British legal connections. Commonwealth and state powers were distinct. Australia adopted the Westminster statute in 1942; the 1939 transition remains outside this editorial core.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Australia — federal constitutional framework after Westminster adoption

politicalStatus.value: Federal constitutional monarchy with Commonwealth legislative autonomy

governments.value: Governor-General, Prime Minister and parliamentary ministry, Senate and House of Representatives

descriptions.value: Adoption in 1942, retrospective to 1939, strengthened Commonwealth legislative autonomy; constitutional and state reservations remained. The later elimination of residual UK links is not backdated. Wartime and state constitutional changes remain partial.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: New Zealand — Dominion parliamentary framework

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing Dominion under the Crown with evolving imperial connections

governments.value: Crown representative, responsible parliamentary ministry, House of Representatives and Legislative Council

descriptions.value: Dominion status in 1907 and the Balfour declaration in 1926 were distinct from Westminster adoption in 1947. Māori political communities are not merged into the later state by labels; local sovereignty and Treaty relationships remain partial.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: New Zealand — unicameral constitutional framework in 1960

politicalStatus.value: Autonomous constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth

governments.value: Governor-General, Prime Minister and cabinet responsible to the House of Representatives

descriptions.value: Westminster was adopted in 1947 and the Legislative Council was abolished from 1 January 1951. A residual UK legislative provision remained until 1986. Modern MMP, electorate numbers and the present monarch are not projected backwards.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Hawaiian Kingdom — Kamehameha’s royal government in 1815

politicalStatus.value: Unified island monarchy

governments.value: King Kamehameha I with royal advisers

descriptions.value: Royal government preceded the 1819 kapu transition and later written constitutions. Unification did not erase island and local political complexity.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Hawaiian Kingdom — royal government around 1880

politicalStatus.value: Independent Hawaiian kingdom

governments.value: King Kalākaua and royal government

descriptions.value: Kalākaua ruled from 1874 to 1891. Royal authority and external relations are supported; the detailed 1864 constitution and franchise remain uncurated. The coerced constitutional change in 1887 and overthrow in 1893 are not projected earlier. The 1900 Kingdom label remains unmapped.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: New South Wales — self-governing British colony

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing British colony

governments.value: Governor, parliamentary ministers, appointed Legislative Council and elected Legislative Assembly

descriptions.value: Responsible government from 1856 coexisted with retained imperial and governor powers. Founding franchise and seat counts are not assumed unchanged. Federation converted the colony to a state in 1901; this core ends before that transition.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Northern Territory — South Australian administration

politicalStatus.value: Territory administered as part of the British colony of South Australia

governments.value: South Australian colonial government and Northern Territory Government Resident

descriptions.value: The territory was not a separate colony with responsible government. Colonial claims and Aboriginal resistance are distinguished. The Commonwealth administrator from 1911 is not projected into 1900; detailed changes in representation remain uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Queensland — self-governing British colony

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing British colony

governments.value: Governor, nominated Legislative Council and elected Legislative Assembly

descriptions.value: The 1859 constitutional framework and bicameral Parliament preceded federation in 1901. Electoral rules changed; the modern unicameral legislature and universal franchise are not projected into this period.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: South Australia — responsible colonial government

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing British colony

governments.value: Colonial government responsible through representative Parliament, under the Crown

descriptions.value: The 1857 constitution and Parliament support a broad core of responsible government. Detailed chambers, franchise and indigenous practical control remain partial. The federal state identity from 1901 lies outside this core.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Victoria — parliamentary British colony

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing British colony with constitutional Parliament

governments.value: Governor and bicameral Legislative Council/Legislative Assembly

descriptions.value: Victoria was a distinct colony from 1851 and had a constitutional bicameral Parliament from 1856. Detailed ministries and franchise remain uncurated. Federation in 1901 is not applied before its effective year.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Western Australia — representative colonial government around 1880

politicalStatus.value: British colony with representative institutions before responsible government

governments.value: Governor with partly elected and partly official/nominated Legislative Council

descriptions.value: The 1870 framework retained the governor’s veto and prorogation powers and a property qualification. The premier and responsible cabinet introduced in 1890 are not projected into 1878 or 1880.

names.value: Western Australia — responsible colonial government in 1900

politicalStatus.value: Self-governing British colony

governments.value: Governor, Premier/ministry, elected Legislative Assembly and elected Legislative Council

descriptions.value: Responsible government began in 1890. The Legislative Council became elective in 1893 and retained a property qualification; its initial nominated membership is not projected into 1900. Federation took effect on 1 January 1901.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: Gilbert and Ellice Islands — colonial framework in 1938

politicalStatus.value: British Crown colony within the Western Pacific administrative system

governments.value: Resident Commissioner under the Western Pacific High Commissioner

descriptions.value: Distinct island and district arrangements and contested outer-island claims remain partial. Independent Kiribati and Tuvalu are not used as historical fallbacks. This core precedes the Pacific war and later separation.

names.value: Guam — US naval administration in 1938

politicalStatus.value: US island dependency administered by the Navy

governments.value: US naval administration

descriptions.value: The 1898 cession and naval administration are supported. The 1950 Organic Act, Interior supervision and later civil regimes are not projected into 1938. Naval officeholders and detailed local powers remain uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: New Caledonia — French colonial framework in 1938

politicalStatus.value: French colony

governments.value: French colonial administration

descriptions.value: France claimed possession in 1853; colonial status continued until 1946. Colonisation involved restrictions on Kanak land. Later overseas territorial status and present autonomous institutions are not projected into 1938. Detailed governor and council powers remain uncurated.

existence.note: Editorial partial coverage, not full political lifetime; exclusive endpoints are coverage bounds.

names.value: New Hebrides — Anglo-French condominium in 1938

politicalStatus.value: Joint British and French colonial condominium

governments.value: British and French Resident Commissioners ruling jointly, with parallel administrations and a Joint Court

descriptions.value: British, French and joint law coexisted. Separate community services did not divide political sovereignty by geometry. The 1957 advisory council, 1975 assembly and independent Vanuatu from 1980 are outside this core.

names.value: New South Wales — gubernatorial colony in 1815

politicalStatus.value: British colonial dependency

governments.value: Governor exercising colonial executive authority

descriptions.value: Restoration of gubernatorial power from 1810 preceded the advisory council in 1823 and responsible government in 1856. The colonial claim does not imply uniform control or consensual extinguishment of indigenous sovereignty.

names.value: Saipan — Japanese South Seas administration in 1938

politicalStatus.value: Island administered by Japan under the League mandate framework

governments.value: Japanese South Seas administration

descriptions.value: Japan administered Saipan under the Class C mandate awarded in 1920 and announced withdrawal from the League in 1933. This announcement is not treated as the effective withdrawal date or as formal termination of the mandate. Japanese practical control in 1938 is supported; consensual annexation is not claimed. Postwar US trusteeship and the present Commonwealth are not used as fallbacks. Specific civil office powers remain uncurated.

sources.usage: Read historical administrative body 75–137: Navy authority 1900, Governor office 1900–61,Native Affairs 1903–1931, later judiciary changes and transfer order 1951. Detailed Fono powers/membership not inferred from records-date ranges.

sources.title: Departmental Manual575DM1 — Introduction and History
sources.usage: Read PDF 0–3 historical subsections Guam/American Samoa/Trust Territory: Guam Navy 1898 then Interior 1950; American Samoa Navy 19 February 1900, Tutuila cession 17 April 1900/Manuʻa 16 July 1904,Congress 1929, Interior 1951. Orders issuance not mistaken for transfer effective days; modern elected regimes and post 1947 Saipan trusteeship not projected into 1938.

sources.institution: Manatū Taonga, Ministry for Culture and Heritage
sources.title: Niue achieves self-government
sources.usage: Read entire historical body 7–12: British protectorate 1900, annexed by NZ 1901, resident commissioner, declined offered autonomy 1965 until self-government 1974. Pre 1900 monarchy/chiefly sovereignty not inferred from modern territorial name.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Tonga — historical recognition and treaties
sources.usage: Read historical body 4–5,13–15,42–44: George Tupou I united Tonga 1845, constitutional monarchy 1875;1900 protected status with UK foreign-affairs control, later growing internal intervention;1920 British treaty termination on King behalf. British colony or unchanging full autonomy not claimed.

sources.institution: Tonga National Commission for UNESCO / World Heritage Centre
sources.title: Ancient Capitals of the Kingdom of Tonga, tentative-list submission
sources.usage: Read historical Description body 84–104: Tuʻi Tonga traditions/royal tombs, traditional genealogies, medieval maritime authority and archaeological uncertainties. Heritage nomination is not a legal sovereignty endorsement and does not establish continuing unified empire 1800/1815; later Kingdom not substituted.

sources.title: The rise of the Mau and the fall of colonial rule in Sāmoa
sources.usage: Read historical body 492–503: old Samoan consular records, German 1900–1914 administration,1899 partition and NZ seizure 1914. German dependency covers western islands, not eastern American Samoa; early island-wide political referent uncurated.

sources.institution: Manatū Taonga, Ministry for Culture and Heritage
sources.title: Capture of German Samoa
sources.usage: Read full Introduction body 7–12: NZ expedition landed 29 August 1914 replacing German administration. Exact day supported, no January 1914 NZ military fallback.

sources.institution: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.title: Apia — Our Story
sources.usage: Read historical body 14–45:1914 military occupation,1920 Class C mandate,1922 colonial powers,1936 change toward Mau, independence 1 January 1962. Conservative 1921 start avoids treating full 1920 as mandated; no 1962 sovereign state projected into 1960.

sources.institution: An Encyclopaedia of New Zealand1966, government historical edition hosted by Manatū Taonga
sources.title: New Zealand’s trusteeship administration of Western Samoa
sources.usage: Read full Steps to Independence body 51–78: civilian administration May 1920/mandate 17 December 1920,1946 UN trusteeship,1947 Assembly/Council of State,1953 Executive Council,1957 ministers,October 1959 cabinet/PM. Racist dismissal of Mau and self-government fitness excluded;August 1960 constitution phrasing conflicts with more precise Parliament account and not accepted as adoption day.

sources.title: History of the Parliament
sources.usage: Read historical body 43–85:1905 German reorganisation,1 May 1920 colonial Legislative Council,1939 Faipule reform,1947 Assembly,1960 Convention August–October and 1962 firstindependent Parliament. No numerical founding council membership assumed unchanged;1962 heads of state/currentparty/leader text excluded.

sources.title: Rapport annuel2017 Wallis-et-Futuna — historical section
sources.usage: Read PDF 18–20 full historical body 468–574: separate 1887 protectorates/unified 5 March 1888,Frenchresident,1942 USbase,1959 referendum but actual 1961 TOMlaw. No 1961 assembly/prefect/1964 districts projected into 1960; earlyislandchiefdoms not collapsed into one polity.

sources.title: PuluwatLighthouseNationalRegisternomination — Japaneseadministrationhistory

Practical Japanese control in 1938 supported; economic modernisation rhetoric, inferred annexation and postwar US trusteeship excluded. Specific 1938 civil office powers uncurated.

limitations: All new entities are partial needs-research/none; no existing enrichment overwritten.
Two wholly unresolved identities retained in mapping review; six additional partially mapped identities have specific reviewed gaps.
Public Queensland/APH HTML access failures were handled with accepted institutional PDF/NMA/AEC bodies; failed sources/snippets not cited as proof.
Production and Git remain untouched by worker; coordinator owns historical review, serial integration, browser rendering, automated tests, commits and push.
historicalCautions: Editorial intervals are partial coverage with exclusive endpoints, not full entity lifetimes.
Colonial legal claims and source descriptions do not establish indigenous consent or uniform effective sovereignty. Māori and other people/community identities receive no automatic political dossier.
Papua administrative union retains separate Papua Crown/New Guinea UNtrust statuses; all earlier generic composite periods remain explicit gaps.
Samoa1914occupation dated29August;1920May–December civilian/pre-mandate gap retained.1960cabinetself-government remains under trusteeship, independent1962heads ofstate/constitution not retrojected.
Wallis/Futuna1959referendum did not establish1961TOMinstitutions in1960. Earlier distinct chieflysystemsnotautomaticallymerged.
AmericanSamoa1900/1904cessionstages and1925Swainsaddition qualify territorial extent.1951order date notassumedtransfer effective day.
Australia1942adoption retroactive1939 notinstant complete independence; NewZealand1947adoption distinct from1907Dominion/1951Councilabolition.
KingdomofHawaii1900 deliberately unresolved; no USterritorialfallback. Institutional introduction reciprocity/Blountchronology contradictions not accepted.
TuʻiTongamedieval/dynasticheritage cannot establish unified1800/1815empire; DutchGuinea1945shortlabel not resolved by Pacific-region placement or geometry.
Japan announced League withdrawal in 1933; this does not establish its effective date or formal termination of the mandate. Saipan’s later US trusteeship is not backdated.
Founding council memberships, franchise and officeholders not assumed unchanged across later years.
Coordinator reuses exact second-tranche archive PDF URL/source ID across Gambia and Fiji; title and usage broadened to the separately body-read Fiji section while retaining Gambia evidence.

scope.title: Pacific/Oceania states and administrations
scope.sourceStrategy: Local archives, Pacific scholarly collections and community-authorised histories; standards and colonial administrations require careful applicability.
scope.priorityRationale: Early source-family batches prioritise long snapshot presence, broad period potential and national archival/constitutional collections. Source availability is a planning expectation, not an entity-by-entity research finding. Families remain indivisible; no periods are researched now.

difficultCases.question: Encoding and accent variants need review; people/land/community labels are not equivalent to the later state.
